bertholomus's two-Spark Beam-1.0-501B-A23B recipe v0.2.0, its default TensorFold lane (beam-1.0-2x-dgx-spark bdfa59fa, tf/; MIT): tensor parallel 2 over the RoCE link, rank 0 serving the OpenAI API, with Reflection's DFlash2 drafter on both ranks. Engine: bertholomus/TensorFold, branch beam-1.0-tp2, at the REV of tf/beam-tf.env (d00201b4, TensorFold 0.6.6 with the beam family), installed on the stock nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3 image the creator runs (the creator publishes no image); the engine's CUDA extensions are built for the GPU present before each rank starts, as tf/beam-tf-build.sh does. Weights: bertholomus/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-EXL3-3bpw-2xGB10 at fb04dd69 (routed experts 3 bits, attention and dense MLPs 6 bits, about 90 GiB per node) and reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2 at 163b276b. Every served setting is the creator's (tf/beam-tf.env): 4-bit drafter weights and draft head, 5 drafts a step adapting between 3 and 5, 16 rows a decode step, the mma3 prompt expert kernel, 4,096-token prompt chunks split in 1,024-row pieces, 4 prompt cache entries, reduce-scatter prompt sums, 4 NCCL channels, the glibc malloc thresholds, 4 sequences decoding together and --context 1,048,576 (Beam's longest, asked). The engine sizes its fp8 KV pool at each start from what a 9 GiB MemAvailable floor leaves, up to that context: the creator's served start held 868,352 positions per node, so the API facts state 868,352 tokens; that is the creator's measurement, not a floor, and the pool can come out larger or smaller on nodes with more or less free memory. Reasoning is always on (Beam always writes its analysis channel); reasoning_effort picks minimal to max (max when unset); tool calls with tool_choice auto, as Beam's harmony format; no structured output (xgrammar is not installed). Deviation from the creator: the image applies one patch to the engine (adapters/beam/bertholomus-tensorfold-tp2/patches/0001-tool-parameters-integral-number-for-integer.patch). Beam's chat template types a JSON-schema integer as number, so the model writes 17.0 and TensorFold's decode_parameter returned the text, a JSON string; on hardware the shared product case returned {"left":"17.0","product":"323.0","right":"19.0"} with a correct answer. With the patch an integral number for an integer parameter comes back as the integer (17); an upstream PR to bertholomus/TensorFold follows once hardware confirms. Not ported: the creator's API key file, 127.0.0.1 listen address, memguard.sh and MIN_START_GIB preflight (platform concerns); the Controller supplies NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME, NCCL_IB_HCA and NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX (the creator's GID 5 is its own nodes'). Memory: each peak is 130,663,231,488 bytes minus the creator's lowest MemAvailable (10,740 MiB head, 11,089 MiB worker) minus the 4,063,231,488-byte idle host use admission charges: 115.34 GB on the entrypoint and 114.97 GB on the worker, estimates until tried here; selected weights per rank (96.9 GB of target plus the 3.9 GB drafter) plus 8 GB overhead are about 108.7 GB, so the load is predicted to fit with the pool taking the rest. Upstream figures (30.6 tok/s decode on ~2K prose, 45.5 tok/s on ~2K code, 64.7 tok/s aggregate over 4 code streams, about 1,400 tok/s cold prefill, KL 0.0121 and 96.87% top-1 agreement against BF16) are the creator's claims, not measured here. The repository's vLLM lane (gb10/, 655,360 tokens) is a different engine and not this recipe. Licences are information only: recipe scripts MIT, TensorFold and the Beam weights Apache-2.0.

display.description: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on four DGX Sparks with KindlingAI's gr8, a from-scratch CUDA inference engine (no vLLM, PyTorch or NCCL at serve time), at tensor parallel 4 over the ConnectX fabric. The weights are KindlingAI's exlr8 native release: DeepSeek's official weights byte for byte (FP8 trunk, MXFP4 routed experts) in the exlr8 file layout, with Engram on, fp8 KV, the checkpoint's MTP layers drafting, and 32 chats at once, each up to 327,680 tokens (a request holds at most 10 tokens less), every chat slot getting its full KV at boot. The default is the creator's fast mode (TUNE=speed), whose replies are not bit-identical to the exact model's. The recipe runs the creator's published image of commit 4038bf81 (kindlingai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-exlr8-4x-spark, gr8 933c8853) with a placement wrapper that reads the platform's VONK_* environment and uses the release in place from the read-only model mounts (about 509 GB a box: every box reads the whole release, Engram tables included). Engram reads its table rows from disk with gr8's pread pool, because the sandbox blocks io_uring; the creator says the output is the same and measured its numbers with io_uring. Options: speed, long context (16 chats, one up to 1,048,576 tokens) or quality (the exact model, 5 chats); and the loader's gen cache on disk (about 80 GB a box, on by default) for faster later boots. Creator claims, unmeasured here: 137.5 tok/s for one request writing code, 83.9 prose, about 7,700-8,400 tok/s prefill from 32K to 256K, 233 tok/s aggregate at 32 streams; at least 3.25 GiB free a box under load. Thinking is on by default at effort low; a request turns it off with chat_template_kwargs thinking false or reasoning_effort none. Text only: the release's vision tower is not loaded. Licences, for information: weights and engine MIT.

display.description: Unpruned GLM-5.2 (744B total, 40B active; QuantTrio Int4-Int8Mix, compressed-tensors) on four Sparks with vLLM tensor parallel 4 over the native multi-node launcher, a 200,000-token context, FP8 DeepSeek-MLA KV in a fixed 10.95 GB pool, MTP with four drafted tokens, FLASHMLA_SPARSE attention with the Triton sparse-MLA kernels and b12x, and full CUDA graphs. Basis: tonyd2wild's recipe (Apache-2.0; kernels from CosmicRaisins/glm-5.2-gb10, mods from ciprianveg, decode-aware scheduler by penguinchang, all Apache-2.0) on drowzeys' published probe-modded vLLM ab666069 image, which carries the same tag name upstream builds locally; upstream's run-time kernel bind mounts are copied into the image at build time. Related recipes for this model and Spark count: glm-5-2-quanttrio-vllm-four (drowzeys kit) and the same creator's NVFP4-KV variant. Upstream figures (32.5 tok/s mean, 36 peak single stream) are claims until measured here. Memory follows the creator's settings: gpu-memory-utilization 0.91 beside the fixed 10.95 GB FP8 KV pool and a 200,000-token context, as in tonyd2wild's launch.sh at 162d7a76 (lines 208 and 209); with a fixed pool the utilization is vLLM's startup free-memory check, and upstream rejects 0.90 explicitly (README line 367). Upstream runs with 0.6 to 0.9 GB of MemAvailable and 3.6 to 4.5 GB of swap in steady state (README lines 342-345). The declared peak is the per-rank loading floor: the weights, the pool and 8 GB of runtime overhead; the reserve is 8 GB, and admission keeps the platform memory floor free beside the peak.
display.title: GLM 5.2 QuantTrio 200K MTP vLLM four Sparks

display.description: GLM-5.3-Flash on two DGX Sparks with TensorFold's native Zig/CUDA server (TensorFold 1.3.0, upstream 81de26f6 plus MiaAI-Lab's 16 engine patches), one rank per Spark over the ConnectX-7 link with RoCE all-gathers that use both PCIe links of the cabled QSFP port when the platform's fabric setup passes both RoCE devices (the engine takes up to two from NCCL_IB_HCA). Serves MiaAI-Lab's EXL3 4 bpw TensorFold checkpoint (EXL3 routed experts, BF16 elsewhere; Mia-AiLab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-4bpw-TensorFold at the revision the kit pins) with the kit's served settings: a 1,048,576-token window, 8 concurrent requests sharing an FP8 KV pool of 512-row pages, 8-bit dense and head weights, DFlash2 drafts at 4 bits, image input (up to 50 images a request; the default image has no video runtime), tool calling and structured outputs, a default reply budget of 32,768 tokens, thinking off by default with reasoning effort Max when a request turns it on, and earlier turns' reasoning dropped from the prompt. Based on MiaAI-Lab's GLM-5.3-Flash DGX Sparks kit 1104 at commit a691916c (Apache-2.0), which supersedes her earlier two-Spark TensorFold kit; the creator publishes no image of it, so the recipe builds her Dockerfile (CUDA 13.3.1, Zig 0.17.0, sm_121) with her patches vendored, with a baseline-CPU Zig target because the image is built on a hosted arm64 runner, and without her optional video runtime. The kit's single-stream and aggregate rates, prefill rates and memory figures are upstream claims, not measured here; per Spark the kit's README names about 83.3 GiB of model, 12.5 GiB of KV pool, 3.6 GiB of prompt cache and a 9.5 GiB reserve kept free as its measured served configuration. The recipe keeps that 9.5 GiB reserve rather than the kit's newer 6.5 GiB: the creator calls the 6.5 GiB and 5 GiB pair predicted and not measured yet, and a 6.5 GiB reserve would leave MemAvailable under the platform memory guard's 8 GiB threshold. Licences, for information: the quantization is Apache-2.0 per the kit's NOTICE, with Z.AI's MIT licence kept for the base model; the DFlash2 drafter is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial) and is not used with the MTP drafter option. Thinking is chosen per request: a request can set reasoning_effort or chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking, and reasoning comes back in reasoning_content.

display.description: vcruz305's one-Spark GLM-5.3-Flash lane on SGLang v0.5.22 (GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-SAGE-SGLang-Spark-recipe at 362fe245, PROFILE=single): r0b0tlab's EXL3 SAGE pack at about 2.25 bits per weight (98.5 GB, mul1 codebook, mixed K3/K4 tiles) with Enntity's DFlash2 draft (4 draft tokens, bf16) through the creator's exllamav3 fork (CoopMK kernels, built for sm_121a) and sglang-exl3 plugin, his eight SGLang patches and a fail-closed flashinfer stub. Deviation from the creator: our patch 0009 is added because the first non-greedy request (temperature above 0) killed the engine with RuntimeError: flashinfer is disabled in this image (fail-closed stub): flashinfer.sampling.top_p_renorm_probs; the patch switches the DFlash verify sampling to SGLang's own torch and triton fallbacks, and the creator only ran greedy. DSA attention on the triton backends, bfloat16 KV cache, CUDA graph for decode batch 1, 8192-token context, one concurrent request, text only (--language-only; the pack's vision tower is not loaded), chunked prefill 4096. The launcher builds the creator's config view (the pack's tensor manifest merged into config.json) under the writable cache, as his make_view.py does. The creator passes no reasoning or tool-call parser, so reasoning text arrives in content and tool calls are not parsed; this recipe mirrors that. Upstream claims, not measured here: single-stream decode mean 28.6 tok/s on his first pass and 27.3 on the second (prose 20.6, code 31.2, json 26.2, math 36.4), prefill 560 tok/s at 4,027 tokens, 24.6 tok/s aggregate for one request in his concurrent profile, about 98 GB on the GPU and a host MemAvailable minimum of 12.4 to 12.6 GB while serving; the first request after start took 37 to 220 s in his boots. The creator marks replay through his own scripts as TODO(confirm): the measured runs used a local image with the same sources mounted over an older bundled exllamav3. The 118.26 GB peak is the Spark's total memory less his reported MemAvailable minimum of 12.4 GB, not measured here. Licences are informational: the recipe repository is Apache-2.0, the pack and GLM-5.3-Flash are MIT, the draft is Apache-2.0.

display.description: Single-DGX-Spark vLLM TP1 + MTP3 profile for the 99 GiB Mia mirror of the local-inference-lab Qwen3.8 Flash Next NVFP4 checkpoint (text, image and video). The 27 GiB PLE table is served from a memory-mapped packed file built once into the platform cache, so it stays evictable page cache. The adapter bakes MiaAI-Lab's PLE offload, MXFP8, QSA FP8-KV, reduced-vocabulary MTP drafting and block-drop patches into the pinned arm64 image. Defaults follow upstream: 262144 context, FP8 KV, BF16 recurrent state, MTP 3, four sequences, 2048-token prefill chunks; contexts up to 524288 use YaRN. GPU memory utilisation 0.786 follows the current upstream .env.sample budget for KV_TARGET_GIB=20, HOST_RESERVE_GIB=26, and a 121.69 GiB host (95.60 GiB budget); it is derived from that owning profile, not a measured constant. The README's 0.780 (94.87 GiB) table documents an earlier KV_TARGET_GIB=16, five-sequence profile. Upstream claims (not measured here): 48.7 tok/s single stream; 162.9 tok/s aggregate needs 8 streams (upstream ran max-num-seqs 8 with a 28 GiB reserve, this recipe defaults to 4). GB10 memory correction: Per-node peak budgets utilization × 130,663,231,488-byte unified memory plus at least 8 GB for CUDA context/graphs, FlashInfer workspace, auxiliary heads and CPU/mmap buffers; 8 GB reserve, with a separate 6 GB OS floor. This is a conservative budget, not a measured footprint.

display.description: Qwen's text-to-speech model with nine built-in voices on one DGX Spark, served by vLLM-Omni 0.34.0 the way the Qwen3-TTS README points to. It answers the OpenAI speech route, POST /v1/audio/speech: pick a voice, optionally give an instruction for style or emotion and a speed, and receive wav, pcm, flac, mp3 or opus. Voice design and voice cloning are not on this route; they stay in the Qwen3-TTS job recipe. The deploy config is the creator's, verified by its authors only on an H100; its two stages (talker and codec decoder) each take the creator's 24 GiB converted to 0.197 of a Spark, so the 64 GB peak is an estimate until tried. Apache-2.0 weights.

display.description: Sage S2.1 Flash (Shanghai AI Laboratory's model on the GLM-5.3-Flash architecture) on four DGX Sparks with KindlingAI's gr8, a from-scratch CUDA inference engine (no vLLM, PyTorch or NCCL at serve time), at tensor parallel 4 over the ConnectX fabric. The weights are KindlingAI's exlr8 K4 release (every routed and shared expert at 4 bits a weight), int4 KV, eight requests at once (SESS=8) sharing a 262,208-token KV pool, requests up to 262,144 tokens, bit-exact shared-waterfill MTP=2 drafting and a prompt cache on disk, text only by default. The kit (kindlingai/sage-s2.1-flash-exlr8-4x-spark at 1f106277) publishes no image, so the recipe follows its own image path: gr8's published image of the kit's gr8 commit ca7e8745 plus the kit's knobs, entrypoint and prompt-cache file, with a placement wrapper that reads the platform's VONK_* environment and uses the release in place from the read-only model mounts. Options: speed, long context (a 2,097,152-token pool, requests up to 1,048,576 tokens, context-parallel KV, experimental upstream) or quality (strict MTP=1); and image input (the creator's untested opt-in). Creator claims, unmeasured here: 88.0 tok/s for one request writing code, 2,999 tok/s prefill at 8K, 79.5 / 106.7 / 127.5 / 162.0 tok/s aggregate at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 streams, 46.5-48.2 GiB free a box with long context. Each box mounts the whole release less the other ranks' index slices (about 165 GB), where the creator's launcher range-fetches about 47 GB from Hugging Face. The model always thinks: a request that turns thinking off gets the template's lowest effort with the reasoning withheld, and a small max_tokens can end inside the thinking. Licence, for information: MIT.

display.description: Single-DGX Spark DiffSynth disk-offload variant of Wan-Dancer's global-planning and local-refinement pipeline. Pinned DiffSynth-Studio disk-maps each safetensors expert, uses a 64 GiB device-residency threshold, and runs the two stages in separate processes. Generation is bounded to 921,600 pixels. The declared 126 GB memory envelope fits Controller admission; prefer the original recipe unless the larger canvas is needed.
